commands.title: Show a service's status
commands.description: Shows whether the service is running, its main PID and its most recent log lines.

commands.title: Start a service
commands.description: Starts the service now; it will not start at boot unless it is also enabled.

commands.title: Stop a service
commands.description: Stops the running service; it stays enabled and returns at the next boot.

commands.title: Restart a service
commands.description: Stops and starts the service, dropping active connections.

commands.title: Reload a service's configuration
commands.description: Asks the service to re-read its config without dropping connections; not every unit supports it.

commands.title: Enable a service and start it now
commands.description: Makes the service start at boot and starts it immediately.

commands.title: Disable a service and stop it now
commands.description: Stops the service and prevents it from starting at boot.

commands.title: Check if a service is running
commands.description: Prints active, inactive or failed and exits non-zero when the service is not active; handy in scripts.

commands.title: Check if a service starts at boot
commands.description: Prints enabled, disabled, masked or static for the unit.

commands.title: List failed units
commands.description: Shows every unit that is in a failed state; check this first after a bad boot.

commands.title: List all running services
commands.description: Shows the services that are currently running.

commands.title: List installed unit files
commands.description: Shows every installed service and whether it is enabled, disabled or static.

commands.title: Reload systemd after editing unit files
commands.description: Makes systemd re-read unit files; required after creating or changing a .service file.

commands.title: Show a unit's full file
commands.description: Prints the unit file and any drop-in overrides that apply to it.

commands.title: Override a unit with a drop-in
commands.description: Opens an override file that survives package updates; run daemon-reload if prompted, then restart the service.

commands.title: Reset a failed unit
commands.description: Clears the failed state so the unit can be started again after hitting the restart limit.

commands.title: Mask a service
commands.description: Links the unit to /dev/null so it cannot be started by anyone or any dependency; undo with unmask.

commands.title: Show the boot time breakdown
commands.description: Lists units by how long they took to start, slowest first.

commands.title: Reboot the server
commands.description: Restarts the machine; every SSH session, including this one, is dropped.

commands.title: Follow a service's logs
commands.description: Streams new log lines for the unit as they arrive; press Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.title: Show a service's recent logs
commands.description: Prints the last 100 log lines for the unit.

commands.title: Show logs since a time
commands.description: Shows everything logged since the given time; accepts values like yesterday or 2025-01-31 10:00.

commands.title: Show logs for a time window
commands.description: Limits output to a window, using a format such as 2025-01-31 09:00:00 for both ends.

commands.title: Show errors from this boot
commands.description: Shows only error and more severe messages since the last boot.

commands.title: Show logs from the previous boot
commands.description: Shows the whole log of the previous boot; useful after a crash or unexpected reboot.

commands.title: Show the latest journal entries
commands.description: Prints the 50 most recent entries from every unit.

commands.title: Follow the whole journal
commands.description: Streams new entries from every service as they are written.

commands.title: Show how much disk the journal uses
commands.description: Prints the total size of archived and active journal files.

commands.title: Shrink the journal to a size
commands.description: Deletes the oldest archived journal files until the total is under the size.

commands.title: Delete journal entries older than a period
commands.description: Removes archived journal files older than the given time.

commands.title: Show kernel messages from the journal
commands.description: Shows only kernel messages for the current boot.

commands.title: Show kernel ring buffer with timestamps
commands.description: Prints kernel messages with human-readable times; good for hardware, disk and OOM issues.

commands.title: Follow the system log
commands.description: Streams the general system log on Ubuntu; press Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.title: Follow the authentication log
commands.description: Streams logins, sudo use and SSH attempts on Debian and Ubuntu.

commands.title: Show recent logins
commands.description: Lists the last 20 logins and reboots from /var/log/wtmp.

commands.title: Show failed login attempts
commands.description: Lists the last 20 failed logins from /var/log/btmp.

commands.title: Find the Out-Of-Memory killer in the logs
commands.description: Shows when the kernel killed a process because the machine ran out of memory.

commands.title: Test the Nginx configuration
commands.description: Checks the config for syntax errors; always run before reloading.

commands.title: Dump the full effective configuration
commands.description: Tests the config and prints it with every included file, handy for support and debugging.

commands.title: Reload Nginx
commands.description: Applies config changes gracefully without dropping connections.

commands.title: Restart Nginx
commands.description: Fully restarts Nginx, which drops active connections; prefer reload for config changes.

commands.title: Show Nginx's status
commands.description: Shows whether Nginx is running and its latest log lines.

commands.title: Test and reload Nginx in one go
commands.command: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
commands.description: Reloads only if the config test passes, so a typo cannot take the site down.

commands.title: Enable a site
commands.description: Links a server block into sites-enabled; test and reload afterwards.

commands.title: Disable a site
commands.description: Removes the symlink only; the file in sites-available is kept. Reload Nginx afterwards.

commands.title: List available and enabled sites
commands.description: Shows which server blocks exist and which are linked as enabled.

commands.title: Follow the access log
commands.description: Streams incoming requests as they are logged.

commands.title: Follow the error log
commands.description: Streams Nginx errors such as upstream failures and permission problems.

commands.title: Show Nginx version and build options
commands.description: Prints the version, compiler flags and compiled-in modules.

commands.title: Count requests per IP
commands.command: sudo awk '{print $1}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
commands.description: Lists the 20 busiest client addresses in the access log.

commands.title: Find 5xx responses in the access log
commands.description: Shows the last 50 requests answered with a server error, assuming the default log format.

commands.title: List the most requested URLs
commands.command: sudo awk '{print $7}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
commands.description: Shows which paths are hit most often.

commands.title: Count responses by status code
commands.description: Summarises how many 200s, 404s, 500s and so on were served.

commands.title: Find which process is using port 80
commands.description: Shows the process listening on port 80, useful when Nginx fails to start.

commands.title: Test the Apache configuration
commands.description: Checks the config for syntax errors; look for Syntax OK before reloading.

commands.title: Enable a site
commands.description: Enables a virtual host from sites-available; reload Apache afterwards.

commands.title: Disable a site
commands.description: Disables a virtual host; its file stays in sites-available. Reload Apache afterwards.

commands.title: Enable a module
commands.description: Enables an Apache module such as rewrite, ssl or headers; restart Apache afterwards.

commands.title: Disable a module
commands.description: Disables an Apache module; restart Apache afterwards.

commands.title: Reload Apache
commands.description: Applies config changes gracefully without dropping connections.

commands.title: Restart Apache
commands.description: Fully restarts Apache, dropping active connections; needed after enabling modules.

commands.title: Show virtual hosts and ports
commands.description: Lists the parsed virtual hosts, their config files and the listening ports.

commands.title: List loaded modules
commands.description: Shows every static and shared module Apache has loaded.

commands.title: Follow the Apache error log
commands.description: Streams errors such as PHP failures and permission problems.

commands.title: Follow the Apache access log
commands.description: Streams incoming requests as they are logged.

commands.title: Get a certificate for Nginx
commands.description: Requests a Let's Encrypt certificate and edits the Nginx config to use it; the domain must point at this server.

commands.title: Get a certificate for Apache
commands.description: Requests a Let's Encrypt certificate and edits the Apache config to use it.

commands.title: Get a certificate with the webroot method
commands.description: Obtains a certificate without changing server config; the web server must serve the webroot.

commands.title: Test certificate renewal
commands.description: Simulates renewal of all certificates against the staging server without changing anything.

commands.title: Renew all certificates
commands.description: Renews any certificate close to expiry; normally done automatically by a timer.

commands.title: List certbot certificates
commands.description: Shows each certificate, its domains, expiry date and file paths.

commands.title: Delete a certificate
commands.description: Removes the certificate and its renewal config; update the web server config first or it will fail to start.

commands.title: Show a certificate's validity dates
commands.description: Prints the notBefore and notAfter dates of a certificate file.

commands.title: Show a certificate's full details
commands.description: Prints the subject, issuer, SANs, key size and extensions of a certificate.

commands.title: Inspect a remote server's certificate
commands.description: Opens a TLS connection and prints the certificate chain; the servername selects the right virtual host.

commands.title: Check a remote certificate's expiry
commands.description: Prints when the certificate served by a remote host starts and expires.

commands.title: Generate a private key and CSR
commands.description: Creates a 2048-bit key without a passphrase and a signing request to send to a certificate authority.

commands.title: Create a self-signed certificate
commands.description: Creates a key and a one-year self-signed certificate; browsers will warn unless you trust it.

commands.title: Check that a key and certificate match
commands.description: Compares the RSA modulus of both files; any difference means they do not belong together. Needs bash or zsh.

commands.title: Export a certificate to PKCS#12
commands.description: Bundles a key and certificate into a .p12 file, asking for an export password.

commands.title: Verify a certificate chain
commands.description: Checks that the certificate was issued by the given CA bundle.

commands.title: Check whether a certificate expires soon
commands.description: Exits non-zero if the certificate expires within 30 days (2592000 seconds); useful in scripts.

commands.title: Show UFW status in detail
commands.description: Shows whether UFW is active, default policies and all rules.

commands.title: List UFW rules with numbers
commands.description: Shows rules with index numbers, which ufw delete needs.

commands.title: Allow SSH through UFW
commands.description: Opens port 22; do this before enabling UFW on a remote server or you will lock yourself out.

commands.title: Allow a port
commands.description: Opens a TCP port to everyone.

commands.title: Allow a port from one IP
commands.command: sudo ufw allow from <ip> to any port <port> proto tcp
commands.description: Opens a TCP port only to the given address.

commands.title: Allow Nginx web traffic
commands.description: Opens ports 80 and 443 using the Nginx application profile.

commands.title: Deny a port
commands.description: Blocks incoming traffic on the port.

commands.title: Delete a UFW rule by number
commands.description: Removes the rule with that index from ufw status numbered; later numbers shift.

commands.title: Rate-limit SSH connections
commands.description: Denies an address that makes 6 or more connections in 30 seconds, slowing brute-force attacks.

commands.title: Enable UFW
commands.description: Turns the firewall on and at boot; allow SSH first or you can lock yourself out.

commands.title: Disable UFW
commands.description: Turns the firewall off, leaving the server exposed.

commands.title: Reset UFW to defaults
commands.description: Deletes every rule and disables UFW.

commands.title: List iptables rules
commands.description: Shows all chains with packet counts, numeric addresses and rule numbers.

commands.title: Accept a port with iptables
commands.description: Appends a rule that accepts TCP traffic on the port; it is lost on reboot unless saved.

commands.title: Flush all iptables rules
commands.description: Removes every rule in the filter table; if the default policy is DROP this locks you out.

commands.title: Show firewalld rules
commands.description: Shows the active zone, its services, ports and rules on RHEL-based systems.

commands.title: Open a port in firewalld
commands.description: Adds the port to the permanent config; it applies after a reload.

commands.title: Reload firewalld
commands.description: Applies permanent changes to the running firewall.

commands.title: Show Fail2ban status
commands.description: Lists the active jails.

commands.title: Show banned IPs in the SSH jail
commands.description: Shows failed and currently banned addresses for the sshd jail.

commands.title: Unban an IP in Fail2ban
commands.description: Removes the address from the sshd jail's ban list.

commands.title: Add a user
commands.description: Creates the user, home directory and group interactively.

commands.title: Add a user to the sudo group
commands.description: Gives the user admin rights; the -a is essential or existing groups are replaced.

commands.title: Add a user to the docker group
commands.description: Lets the user run Docker without sudo, which is effectively root access; they must log in again.

commands.title: Delete a user and their home
commands.description: Removes the account and its home directory and mail spool permanently.

commands.title: Change a user's password
commands.description: Sets a new password for the user.

commands.title: Show a user's password aging
commands.description: Shows when the password was changed and when it expires.

commands.title: Show a user's ID and groups
commands.description: Prints the UID, GID and every group the user belongs to.

commands.title: List a user's groups
commands.description: Prints the groups the user belongs to.

commands.title: Show logged-in users
commands.description: Lists who is logged in, from which terminal and since when.

commands.title: Show what logged-in users are doing
commands.description: Shows logged-in users, their idle time and the command they are running.

commands.title: Start a root shell
commands.description: Opens a login shell as root with root's environment.

commands.title: Switch to another user
commands.description: Opens a login shell as that user.

commands.title: Change owner recursively
commands.description: Gives the user and group ownership of the directory and everything in it.

commands.title: Make a file readable by everyone
commands.description: Owner can read and write; group and others can read.

commands.title: Make a directory or script executable by all
commands.description: Owner has full access; others can read and execute.

commands.title: Make a file private to its owner
commands.description: Only the owner can read and write; required for SSH private keys.

commands.title: Add the execute bit to a file
commands.description: Makes the file executable, such as a script.

commands.title: Find world-writable files
commands.description: Lists files anyone can read, write and execute; usually a misconfiguration.

commands.title: Edit the sudoers file safely
commands.description: Opens sudoers and checks syntax on save so a typo cannot break sudo.

commands.title: Copy your SSH key to a server
commands.description: Installs your public key in the remote authorized_keys so you can log in without a password.

commands.title: Fix SSH directory permissions
commands.description: Sets the strict permissions sshd requires, otherwise key login silently fails.

commands.title: Look up a user in the account database
commands.description: Shows the user's passwd entry, including LDAP or other sources.

commands.title: List all human users
commands.description: Prints accounts with regular user IDs.

commands.title: Update and upgrade all packages
commands.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
commands.description: Refreshes the package index and installs available updates.

commands.title: Refresh the package index
commands.description: Downloads the latest package lists without installing anything.

commands.title: Install a package
commands.description: Installs the package and its dependencies.

commands.title: Remove a package
commands.description: Removes the package but keeps its configuration files.

commands.title: Purge a package
commands.description: Removes the package and its system-wide configuration files.

commands.title: Remove unused dependencies
commands.description: Removes packages that were installed as dependencies and are no longer needed.

commands.title: List installed packages
commands.description: Prints every installed package with its version.

commands.title: List upgradable packages
commands.description: Shows packages that have a newer version available.

commands.title: Search for a package
commands.description: Searches package names and descriptions.

commands.title: Show package details
commands.description: Shows the version, dependencies, size and description of a package.

commands.title: Show candidate versions of a package
commands.description: Shows the installed version, the candidate and which repository provides each.

commands.title: Check if a package is installed
commands.description: Lists installed packages whose names match; ii at the start means installed.

commands.title: List files installed by a package
commands.description: Prints every file the installed package put on disk.

commands.title: Find which package owns a file
commands.description: Tells you which installed package a file belongs to.

commands.title: Hold a package at its current version
commands.description: Stops the package from being upgraded or removed until released.

commands.title: Release a held package
commands.description: Allows the package to be upgraded again.

commands.title: Show held packages
commands.description: Lists packages that are on hold.

commands.title: Dry-run unattended upgrades
commands.description: Shows which security updates would be installed automatically without applying them.

commands.title: Install a package with dnf
commands.description: Installs a package on Fedora, RHEL 8+ and derivatives.

commands.title: Update all packages with dnf
commands.description: Updates every installed package on Fedora, RHEL 8+ and derivatives.

commands.title: Install a package with yum
commands.description: Installs a package on CentOS 7 and older RHEL systems.

commands.title: Update all packages with yum
commands.description: Updates every installed package on CentOS 7 and older RHEL systems.

commands.title: Install a snap
commands.description: Installs a snap package from the Snap Store.

commands.title: List installed snaps
commands.description: Shows installed snaps with version and revision.

commands.title: Refresh all snaps
commands.description: Updates every installed snap to its latest version.

commands.title: List your cron jobs
commands.description: Prints the current user's scheduled jobs.

commands.title: Edit your cron jobs
commands.description: Opens your crontab in an editor; format is minute hour day month weekday command.

commands.title: Remove all your cron jobs
commands.description: Deletes the whole crontab immediately with no confirmation.

commands.title: List another user's cron jobs
commands.description: Prints the scheduled jobs of the given user.

commands.title: Edit another user's cron jobs
commands.description: Opens the given user's crontab in an editor.

commands.title: List systemd timers
commands.description: Shows scheduled systemd timers, when they last ran and when they run next.

commands.title: Show cron activity in the log
commands.description: Shows the last cron job executions on Debian and Ubuntu.

commands.title: Preview scripts that cron.daily would run
commands.description: Lists the scripts that would run without executing them.

commands.title: List system cron jobs
commands.description: Shows system-wide cron files in addition to user crontabs.

commands.title: List PM2 processes
commands.description: Shows every process PM2 manages with status, CPU, memory and restarts.

commands.title: Start an app with PM2
commands.description: Starts a script under PM2 and gives it a name.

commands.title: Restart a PM2 app
commands.description: Stops and starts the app, causing brief downtime.

commands.title: Reload a PM2 app with zero downtime
commands.description: Restarts cluster-mode workers one by one so the app keeps serving.

commands.title: Stop a PM2 app
commands.description: Stops the app but keeps it in the PM2 list.

commands.title: Delete a PM2 app
commands.description: Stops the app and removes it from PM2's list.

commands.title: Show PM2 logs
commands.description: Streams the app's output and error logs; omit the name for all apps.

commands.title: Open the PM2 monitor
commands.description: Shows a live dashboard of CPU, memory and logs per process.

commands.title: Save the PM2 process list
commands.description: Stores the current list so it can be restored after a reboot.

commands.title: Make PM2 start at boot
commands.description: Prints a command to run with sudo that installs a boot service; run pm2 save afterwards.

commands.title: Restore saved PM2 processes
commands.description: Starts the processes stored by pm2 save.

commands.title: Show details of a PM2 app
commands.description: Prints script path, environment, restart count and log file locations.

commands.title: Clear PM2 logs
commands.description: Empties all PM2 log files.

commands.title: Update PM2 in memory
commands.description: Restarts the PM2 daemon while keeping the saved processes running.

commands.title: Show Supervisor process status
commands.description: Lists every Supervisor program and whether it is running.

commands.title: Restart a Supervisor program
commands.description: Stops and starts the program.

commands.title: Load new Supervisor config
commands.command: sudo supervisorctl reread && sudo supervisorctl update
commands.description: Reads changed config files and starts or stops programs to match.

commands.title: Follow a Supervisor program's output
commands.description: Streams the program's stdout; add stderr at the end for its error output.
